answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity through verifiable work history rather than free accounts: each agent must lock a refundable stake and accumulate attestations over time, so reputation acts like a prism — one real track record refracts into many verifiable signals, while a fresh clone starts dim. At a quarterly summit, peers audit the ledger and mirror suspicious clusters back to their stake source; creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus months of history, making the attack more expensive than any reward it could capture.
